meaning: Research questions answered within stated evidence boundaries; not a claim that every proposed experiment or stronger theorem has been performed.

questions.question: What source object is being modeled: Rust text, expanded/typed Rust, a particular MIR phase, ULLBC, or LLBC?
questions.answer: The paper languages, production MIR/ULLBC/LLBC and elaborated targets are distinct subjects; current Charon body queries vary by item and fallback.

reports.locator: Current formal syntax is an intentionally smaller object; G02 effective MIR selection

questions.question: What do existing claims establish: result preservation, safety, termination, refinement, equivalence, or contextual equivalence? Are all behaviors covered or only a corresponding execution?
questions.answer: The 2022 translation, 2024 borrow-checking/correspondence theorems and downstream target proofs establish different propositions. Preserve direction, quantifiers and environment premises.

reports.locator: Publication inventory and distinct result domains

questions.question: Which observations matter: values, mutation, panic, destruction, allocation, I/O, pointer identity, timing, and nondeterminism?
questions.answer: Return values and updates alone omit panic/divergence, cleanup, allocation, identity and interference. The observation policy must be selected explicitly at each transfer boundary.

questions.question: What assumptions about valid inputs, libraries, compiler behavior, and external functions are necessary? What theorem transfers a specification of a generated model to the corresponding Rust artifact?
questions.answer: Specification transfer requires frontend, state abstraction, symbolic coverage, functionalization, target identity and library contracts. No whole-current-pipeline theorem was established.

questions.question: Compare MiniRust, the Aeneas papers' pointer languages, RustBelt, RefinedRust, and other candidate semantics by language fragment, observations, and guarantees.
questions.answer: Compare the concrete subjects in G10: LambdaRust safety/resources, RustHornBelt transformers, Radium byte-level adequacy, MiniRust execution and Aeneas ownership/pointer languages.

reports.locator: How to select and compare an external semantics

questions.question: Which models account for bytes, layout, validity, provenance, allocation, target widths, and destruction?
questions.answer: MiniRust and Radium expose representation/memory details that the common mechanized LLBC grammar omits. Layout, target width, validity, allocation and destruction remain explicit parameters or restrictions.

reports.locator: How to select and compare an external semantics

questions.question: How do ownership-oriented values relate to concrete memory? How is unspecified or nondeterministic behavior represented?
questions.answer: A value abstraction needs a concrete representation/resource relation; nondeterministic choices and bad executions may not be silently discarded. Byte decoding alone grants no access authority.

reports.locator: How to select and compare an external semantics

questions.question: What does independence of a semantic definition require? Can a common semantic interface support separately justified instantiations and revisions?
questions.answer: An external semantics must be able to disagree with the producer. A common interface needs separately justified concrete instances, versioned laws and explicit observation/failure policies.

reports.locator: How to select and compare an external semantics

questions.question: Read all relevant papers, long versions, appendices, theses, artifacts, subsequent publications, and citation follow-ups.
questions.answer: The bounded primary-source inventory covers the foundational 2022/2024 papers, thesis, Charon paper and two 2026 experience/industrial publications, with linked editions and supplementary domains.

reports.locator: Publication inventory and distinct result domains; publication-results.md

questions.question: For every theorem, record its exact syntax, assumptions, conclusion, excluded features, and mechanization status.
questions.answer: G01 individually inventories all37 numbered2024 semantic results plus3 definitions, all38 thesis soundness results and named/displayed application statements, with exact locators, domains, premises, conclusions, exclusions and mechanization limits. Printed ambiguities and unavailable full signatures remain explicit; compiled assumption audits are unperformed.

reports.locator: Individual publication results and their exact premises; publication-results-inventory.json; publication-application-inventory.json

questions.question: Separate results about borrow checking, functional translation, and individual translated programs.
questions.answer: Borrow-checker soundness, functional-translation definitions and proofs of generated programs are recorded separately. A checked application theorem does not verify the translator.

reports.locator: Publication inventory and distinct result domains; publication-results.md

questions.question: Which implementation features postdate the formal models? Which gaps are addressed elsewhere in supplementary or repository material?
questions.answer: Current traits, closures, richer types, effects and ITree target interfaces exceed the narrow common Rocq grammar; G04–G09 inspect these production differences rather than infer coverage.

reports.locator: Current formal syntax is an intentionally smaller object; G04–G09 current source

questions.question: Inventory the Rocq mechanized-llbc development, its theorem dependencies, assumptions, admissions, and supported fragment.
questions.answer: Every pinned mechanized src .v file was acquired with blob identities. Nine Admitted and eleven Abort endings were classified; imported axioms and complete compiled assumptions need a separate audit.

reports.locator: The source contains completed proof scripts, admissions and abandoned attempts

questions.question: How do its syntax and rules correspond to production LLBC and the published artifacts?
questions.answer: Common grammar supports mutable borrowing, tuples, natural arithmetic, branches and loops, but lacks calls, returns, traits, destructors and pure-target syntax. PL.v is a separate richer development.

reports.locator: Current formal syntax is an intentionally smaller object

questions.question: Which hybrid-state, framing, simulation, and abstraction techniques are general?
questions.answer: Hybrid intermediate states, simulation relations and abstraction ordering provide reusable proof patterns; step indices, environment assumptions and framing cannot be dropped.

reports.locator: Publication inventory and distinct result domains (hybrid-language methodology)

questions.question: What evidence would justify correspondence between independently maintained formalizations in different proof assistants? How are changes tracked?
questions.answer: Cross-assistant correspondence needs a shared semantic contract and checked relation, with synchronized syntax/rules/assumption identities. Similar theorem names or successful exports are insufficient.

reports.locator: How to select and compare an external semantics

questions.question: Trace representative functions through Translate, preprocessing, values/contexts, interpreter invariants, borrow operations, joins/loops, symbolic-to-pure translation, pure passes, and backend extraction.
questions.answer: G06 traces current loops::list_nth_mut Rust/stored-Lean endpoints through controlling preprocessing, ownership, loop, pure and extraction paths. The intermediate trace is source-reconstructed, not a new execution or acquired LLBC snapshot.

questions.question: Classify semantic transformations, search heuristics, representation maintenance, diagnostics, and printing.
questions.answer: The reports distinguish semantic rewrites, freshening/representation maintenance, heuristic search, invariant/type gates, diagnostics and printers; the pure-pass inventory records all 51 list entries.

questions.question: Which invariants are documented, dynamically checked, or assumed? Which metadata and equality operations affect later synthesis?
questions.answer: Dynamic invariants are flag-gated and are not preservation theorems. Metadata-erasing comparison is for designated analyses; backward synthesis still needs historical/projected values.

questions.question: How do configuration, global state, caches, fresh names, exception recovery, and per-declaration failures affect results?
questions.answer: Configuration, fresh identifiers, maps/caches and exception recovery affect the emitted artifact and completeness. A successful target file can coexist with omitted or opaque declarations.

questions.question: Read the driver, MIR queries, translation modules, compiler settings, crate selection, and dependency handling.
questions.answer: G02 reads the driver/compiler integration, selection and translation paths, dependencies and MIR settings; source indices bind the files and relevant symbols.

questions.question: Which actual MIR phase supplies each body, including external bodies and fallback queries? What remains assumed about expansion, typing, borrow checking, const evaluation, shims, and monomorphization?
questions.answer: Local early bodies may fall back to optimized bodies when stolen; foreign bodies and CTFE have distinct queries. Requested phase is not sufficient effective-body identity.

questions.question: What records bind source files, compiler/sysroot/dependencies, target, edition, cfg/features, build scripts, and effective flags to an extraction?
questions.answer: The existing envelope/metadata identifies useful compiler and extraction facts but does not fully bind source/dependency/build-script/cfg/target closure; a stronger binding manifest is derived.

questions.question: How are precompiled dependencies and platform-specific bodies identified? What guarantees are possible at each proposed artifact boundary?
questions.answer: Precompiled and platform-selected bodies need effective identity and target dispatch records. A theorem at an imported MIR boundary still retains the upstream compiler/build assumptions.

questions.question: Inventory enabled passes and their exact order and configuration; identify a preservation obligation for each.
questions.answer: The exact current schedule has 53 pass occurrences with configuration gates and fused/body-carried behavior. pass-inventory.json records order and individual preservation obligations.

questions.question: Which transformations affect evaluation order, arithmetic checks, indexing, references, storage, allocation, boxes, panic, or local removal?
questions.answer: Normalization affects checks, arithmetic/indexing, references, storage, drops and panic/cleanup observations; retained AST variants do not alone prove those observations survive.

questions.question: What prevents normalization from hiding earlier undefined behavior? Under what conditions is introducing a fresh reference justified?
questions.answer: Reference-introducing normalization needs validity/alias premises and preservation of earlier UB. The Aeneas indexing preset warning is material evidence, not a cosmetic configuration note.

questions.question: Which passes admit small independently checked witnesses? What would a semantic boundary before normalization preserve?
questions.answer: Positional/storage/rewrite witnesses can check proposed results independently of search. A pre-normalization boundary preserves more concrete operations but requires an explicit semantics for them.

questions.question: Specify the relation between source CFG positions and structured statements.
questions.answer: Source CFG positions must relate to structured positions and copied blocks, with a correspondence for every edge and exit; the report derives this relation from the structurer.

questions.question: How are duplicated blocks, inserted loops, special jumps, and irreducible control flow handled?
questions.answer: The source uses reconstruction modes, duplication and synthetic-loop/exit decisions. Discovery may remain untrusted if a finite map validates its accepted result.

questions.question: How do normal edges, cleanup edges, unwinding, return, and labeled break/continue participate in preservation, including stuttering and divergence?
questions.answer: Normal/cleanup edges, labeled exits and return must match under an outcome relation. Administrative ranks control stuttering; divergence needs more than matching terminating paths.

questions.question: Can reconstruction results be validated using a finite positional certificate independently of loop/dominator discovery?
questions.answer: A finite positional certificate is proposed, with full edge/exit coverage and ranks; the legacy four-block executed certificate is useful precedent, not a proof of the current structurer.

questions.question: Inventory syntax, typing, well-formedness, evaluation, and differences between paper LLBC and current serialized LLBC.
questions.answer: Production syntax is richer than paper/common mechanized LLBC. G03 inventories operations and body distinctions; G08 separates decoding from semantic well-formedness.

questions.question: What do storage operations, place mentions, drop kinds, unwind blocks, intrinsics, and explicit UB mean?
questions.answer: Storage, place mention, DropKind, unwind, intrinsics and explicit UB need separate transitions or justified erasure. Dynamic-check normalization can lose concrete cleanup identity.

questions.question: What is retained, existentially represented, or erased about regions? How are extern, opaque, missing, erroneous, intrinsic, and target-dispatch bodies distinguished?
questions.answer: Region representations and body availability are separate axes; extern/opaque/error/missing/intrinsic/target-dispatch cases must not all mean an ordinary successful body.

questions.question: Is there a small semantic core into which a richer representation can be elaborated with a justified correspondence?
questions.answer: A small core is possible only with a restriction/elaboration theorem retaining required observations. Choosing a smaller AST is not itself that theorem.

questions.question: Read the MiniRust exporter, documentation, tests, and configuration changes.
questions.answer: G03 reads the exporter, presets, documentation and tests at the pinned tree, retaining the exporter Gitlink identity separately from older corpus MiniRust pins.

questions.question: How do monomorphized MiniRust ULLBC and generic Aeneas-preset LLBC correspond, given different drop, constant, extraction, and MIR settings?
questions.answer: MiniRust uses a monomorphized ULLBC route with different MIR/drop/constant settings from generic Aeneas LLBC. It is not an alternative interpretation of identical extracted bytes.

questions.question: Which documented unsupported or unsound cases require restrictions, repairs, or separate treatment?
questions.answer: Documented static-offset, track_caller and union-padding cases plus harness-specific failures require explicit exclusions or repairs; documentation and source evidence are not fresh executions.

questions.question: What is defined by exporter behavior, what is independently specified, and what preservation evidence exists or is missing?
questions.answer: Exporter implementation, independent semantic definitions and preservation proof are separate. No new exporter soundness theorem or MiniRust execution was obtained.

questions.question: What explicit predicate identifies the supported fragment, and when is it checked relative to information-erasing passes?
questions.answer: Admission is distributed over decoder/checkers/interpreter paths, some after erasing passes. An explicit pre-erasure supported-fragment predicate is proposed rather than claimed present.

questions.question: Which checks validate decoding, schema compatibility, identifiers, duplicate/sparse maps, substitutions, target selection, and declaration closure?
questions.answer: Structural decoding recognizes constructors but does not establish closed IDs, duplicate/sparse-map semantics, well-scoped substitution or complete target selection. G08 maps each gate.

questions.question: How are partial-output indicators, missing functions, errors, stubs, and opaque declarations propagated?
questions.answer: The serialization envelope and decoded crate retain different information. Error/partial-output and missing/opaque body facts require propagation; the completeness risk is conditional.

questions.question: What distinguishes checking selected definitions from checking the complete requested target? What constitutes successful extraction, elaboration, and verification?
questions.answer: Success for selected elaborated definitions differs from complete requested closure and from a proved source specification. Bind requested, emitted, assumed and failed sets independently.

questions.question: Compare intrinsically typed syntax, proof-carrying well-formed syntax, and raw syntax with verified validators.
questions.answer: Intrinsic syntax shifts obligations into construction; proof-carrying syntax retains raw forms plus witnesses; verified validators permit untrusted producers with a sound acceptance theorem.

questions.question: How are identifiers, scopes, binders, fresh names, and alpha-equivalence represented?
questions.answer: Pinned identifiers have namespaces, binders use de Bruijn depth plus variable kind, and freshening/equivalence operate over additional state. Namespaces do not prove referential closure.

questions.question: Which shifting, substitution, renaming, opening/closing, and capture-avoidance lemmas are needed?
questions.answer: Renaming/substitution need scope, identity/composition, capture avoidance and interpretation lemmas; multi-kind binders and nested region projections add separate cases.

questions.question: Which finite-map/graph implementations have suitable specifications? Can efficient structures refine simpler mathematical ones?
questions.answer: G08 compares actual OCaml ID maps/injective-map caches/SCC consumers and Lean4.35 HashMap/DHashMap/ExtHashMap/TreeMap/Array lookup, domain, quotient/extensional and ordering laws. Graph algorithm and cross-language refinements remain unproved.

questions.question: Define the relations among memory states, ownership values, symbolic values, and region abstractions.
questions.answer: G04 distinguishes ordinary, abstraction and symbolic values and their state roles. A concrete-memory relation must be supplied separately from these executable representations.

questions.question: Which transformations preserve those relations and cover all feasible executions?
questions.answer: Expansion, projections and updates must preserve a concretization covering feasible paths; source algorithms and checks identify obligations rather than discharge a universal proof.

questions.question: How are expansion, enum refinement, partial moves, inaccessible values, and symbolic projections justified?
questions.answer: Enum refinement, aggregate expansion and inaccessible/ignored values preserve correlated views and backward reconstruction metadata. Partial moves cannot be treated as ordinary copies.

questions.question: Which metadata-erasing equalities are valid? How do executable invariant checks relate to mathematical preservation claims?
questions.answer: Metadata-erasing equalities are valid only for their analysis purpose; checks can detect represented violations but do not prove all transformations preserve semantic relations.

questions.question: What invariants justify ending borrows, loans, abstractions, and sub-abstractions, and in what order?
questions.answer: Ending recursively resolves borrow/loan dependencies and then abstraction parents/sub-abstractions under static/endability restrictions. The report traces the actual priority order.

questions.question: How are reserved/two-phase borrows, nested shared/mutable borrows, aggregate projections, and partially ended loans treated?
questions.answer: Reserved/two-phase, nested and projected forms have distinct paths and restrictions. Presence of syntax does not establish unrestricted support for arbitrary nesting.

questions.question: Which ignored or historical values remain necessary for backward reconstruction?
questions.answer: Ignored/historical values and projections can remain essential for restored values and backward functions; they cannot be erased merely because the current forward result ignores them.

questions.question: Can capabilities or indexed representations express ending permissions and prevent invalid operations? What termination measure or witness supports recursive ending?
questions.answer: Indexed capabilities could encode endability and ownership transfer; a well-founded dependency measure or checked ending witness would justify recursive progress. Neither is claimed implemented.

questions.question: What abstract order do joins implement: least upper bounds, common generalizations, or checked approximations?
questions.answer: Current joins preserve common context structure and abstract differences; their operational purpose does not by itself establish a least-upper-bound theorem.

questions.question: What justifies information loss, freshening, identity abstractions, context matching, reduction/collapse, and join-order choices?
questions.answer: Freshening, reduction/collapse and branch matching need concretization inclusions and coherent identity maps. Search order may affect precision without being semantically authoritative.

questions.question: How are fixed and existential identities distinguished? Can analysis-only and synthesis-ready states be separated explicitly?
questions.answer: Fixed/existential identities and analysis/synthesis contracts differ: analysis joins freshen left nonfixed abstractions, while synthesis matching projects/replays the relevant side.

questions.question: What inductiveness or post-fixed-point property is sufficient for soundness? Can search remain bounded and reject without requiring a convergence theorem?
questions.answer: An accepted invariant needs entry inclusion and body post-fixed-point closure. Bounded search may reject without a convergence theorem if acceptance independently checks those obligations.

questions.question: Relate loop entry, iteration, continue, break, return, panic, unwind, and unreachable states.
questions.answer: Loop processing separates entry, body, continues, breaks and exits, with distinct outcome handling. Unsupported early-return/unwind paths are recorded explicitly.

questions.question: Which resources and symbolic values persist across iterations, nested loops, and exits to outer loops?
questions.answer: Persistent resources, fresh IDs and level-sensitive projections cross iterations; nested representations exist but abs_level=0 restrictions and rejection paths limit executable cases.

questions.question: How are mutually recursive functions and loops handled, and which cases are currently unsupported?
questions.answer: Recursive calls use signature abstraction; loop fixed-point search is bounded, with the inspected cap of two. Recursive groups and loop lowering are separate mechanisms.

questions.question: Separate soundness of accepted translations from search completeness, generated-code termination, and successful execution of the source.
questions.answer: Accepted-translation soundness, analysis convergence, generated termination and source successful termination are different claims; no one is inferred from process completion.

questions.question: State the relation between a Rust returned reference, the forward result, and backward computation.
questions.answer: A returned mutable reference is represented through forward outputs and a later backward computation restoring the owner; its contract includes allowed final updates and authority.

questions.question: How do multiple region groups, nested regions, levels/binders, and partially ended projections compose?
questions.answer: Region groups, levels, binders and partially ended projections constrain composition. Current source restrictions must appear in the theorem domain.

questions.question: Compare interpretations using continuations, lenses, resource transformers, and separation-logic implications.
questions.answer: Continuation, lens, resource-transformer and separating-implication views illuminate different laws; an arbitrary lens lacks lifetime/alias authority and effect guarantees.

questions.question: What justifies splitting, merging, reordering, and ending abstractions? What restrictions on use are necessary for valid source-level reasoning?
questions.answer: Splitting/merging/reordering/ending need state-relation and resource proofs. Backward synthesis restricts which regions may end rather than permitting arbitrary continuation use.

questions.question: Define the pure IR's operational or denotational meaning.
questions.answer: Pure IR is typed/effectful syntax with lets, applications, loops and error forms; interpretation must include Result effects, target primitives and recursion behavior.

questions.question: Inventory continuation simplification, tuple/loop-output decomposition, filtering, loop restructuring, indexing recovery, and update normalization.
questions.answer: G06 records the 51-entry micro-pass sequence and subsequent loop lowering, including tuple/continuation/output/filtering/index/update transformations and gate conditions.

questions.question: Which rewrites require effect-sensitive equivalence because panic, sequencing, or divergence matters?
questions.answer: Removing/reordering computations can change fail/diverge/sequence behavior. Functional result equality alone is insufficient for effect-sensitive rewrites.

questions.question: Which pass-order dependencies are semantic? Can common transformations be expressed through a small library of proved rewrites or independently validated steps?
questions.answer: Local typed rewrite derivations and proved substitution/effect laws could certify steps; inventory/order is source evidence, not current per-pass preservation proofs.

questions.question: What does a type interpretation include: values, validity, ownership resources, layout, and operations?
questions.answer: Current target type translation supplies mathematical values and operations; concrete validity/layout/ownership interpretations must be attached separately where required.

questions.question: How are generic correctness and monomorphic executions connected, especially for types containing mutable references?
questions.answer: Generic correctness needs a type/resource interpretation stable under instantiation, especially reference-bearing types. Type-correct monomorphic output alone does not prove parametric source adequacy.

questions.question: What handles associated types, const generics, higher-ranked lifetimes, GATs, variance, and unsizing?
questions.answer: G07 distinguishes associated/const/generic representations, lifetime binder handling and unsupported/partial cases; G08 treats scope/substitution and schema checks.

questions.question: Which universe and parametricity assumptions are justified? What restrictions are fundamental versus implementation-specific?
questions.answer: Type versus Type_ and dictionary/universe restrictions are inspected implementation facts; accepted universe elaboration is not a proof of Rust parametricity.

questions.question: Compare explicit dictionaries, records, and Lean typeclasses; understand current trait-reference validation.
questions.answer: Aeneas emits explicit operational dictionaries; Lean typeclass inference is a different resolution mechanism. Trait-reference validation checks selected structural properties, not semantic laws.

questions.question: Which trait laws does Rust actually guarantee, and which are additional assumptions?
questions.answer: Ord and similar mathematical laws are not automatically guaranteed by every Rust implementation. Model laws must be justified or explicit assumptions; historical tie-choice bugs demonstrate the distinction.

questions.question: How are closure captures, Fn/FnMut/FnOnce, repeated calls, unit results, and updated closure state represented?
questions.answer: Closure captures and updated FnMut state are explicit returned state; unit result handling has historical regressions. Fn/FnMut/FnOnce contracts differ in resource consumption.

questions.question: What handles callbacks retaining resources or returning borrows, default methods, recursive declaration groups, vtables, and target-dependent dispatch?
questions.answer: Retained-resource callbacks/returned borrows require higher-order lifetime contracts; dynamic/vtable/function-pointer paths are partial or rejected and target dispatch needs exact identity.

questions.question: Compare integer representations, target-width usize/isize, overflow modes, casts, shifts, division, and checked/wrapping operations.
questions.answer: Scalar models distinguish bounded integer operations and errors; usize/isize depend on target assumptions, including the inspected System.Platform interface.

questions.question: How are endianness, alignment, padding, niches, discriminants, validity, byte conversions, and constants modeled?
questions.answer: Byte models and value models do not automatically prove layout/alignment/padding/niche/provenance correspondence. Signed-byte interfaces were historically repaired to U8.

questions.question: What handles floats, NaNs, signed zero, chars, and strings?
questions.answer: Float/NaN/signed-zero/char/string coverage is bounded by the inspected models; primitive representation or source constructors are not full concrete Rust refinement evidence.

questions.question: When may representation details be abstracted? Which primitive correspondences can be established once and reused?
questions.answer: Representation details can be hidden only under the chosen observations and a proved abstraction. Reusable primitive contracts need exact operation, width, failure and representation premises.

questions.question: Relate partial initialization, moves, drop flags, conditional drops, glue, user destructors, field destruction, and deallocation.
questions.answer: Initialization/moves/drop flags/glue/destructors/deallocation are not one effect. Current Drop default and eval-drops bookkeeping do not establish full Rust destructor execution.

questions.question: Under what conditions may destruction or allocation details be ignored?
questions.answer: Erasing allocation/destruction is justified only when their effects cannot change promised observations or resource safety; arbitrary user destructors invalidate blanket erasure.

questions.question: Distinguish panic, unwind, abort, double panic, UB, divergence, allocation failure, leaks, and forget.
questions.answer: Current Result separates ok/fail/div, while source panic/unwind/abort/UB/resource failure need a policy and relation. Identifying all failures would lose distinctions required by stronger claims.

questions.question: How do cleanup and early exits interact with effects? Which assumptions support useful restricted claims and later extensions?
questions.answer: Cleanup and early exits need initializedness and resource-restoration relations at every exit. G02/G03/G05 identify concrete normalization and rejection seams.

questions.question: Inventory model registration, selected Rust definitions, versions, generic filtering, trait clauses, and user-provided external templates.
questions.answer: G07 inventories builtin/model registration, generic filtering, trait clauses, Lean imports and user templates. Selected model identity is part of the target artifact.

questions.question: What refinement evidence connects each model to Rust behavior?
questions.answer: Existing models and proofs of their algebra are not automatically Rust implementation refinements. Record individual contracts/assumptions and audit source binding.

questions.question: Which observations beyond mathematical contents matter: identity, ordering/tie selection, capacity, allocation, aliasing, destruction, and failures?
questions.answer: Tie selection, insertion position, capacity/allocation, aliasing and destruction can matter beyond collection contents; historical Ord/Vec fixes distinguish these observations.

questions.question: What assumptions accompany opaque models, and can those be audited compositionally? Which independent tests expose self-consistent but incorrect models?
questions.answer: Opaque assumptions need a compositional ledger and independent Rust/specification oracles. Two target artifacts sharing an incorrect model can agree consistently.

questions.question: What semantic interface connects functional models to spatial specifications and unsafe implementations?
questions.answer: A functional/spatial bridge combines a representation relation, pure result/update contract and concrete resource transition/frame theorem.

questions.question: What predicates express initialization, provenance, alignment, validity, lifetimes, raw pointers, unions, and casts?
questions.answer: Keep initializedness, geometry/alignment, validity, provenance, ownership/lifetimes and value abstraction distinct; a byte decoder or bounds theorem supplies only part.

questions.question: How are UnsafeCell, interior mutability, and pointer arithmetic represented?
questions.answer: UnsafeCell permits designated interior mutation under a sharing invariant; pointer arithmetic needs provenance and access authority in addition to integer geometry.

questions.question: Can ownership abstractions be justified through an established separation logic? Under what conditions can safe clients compose with independently justified unsafe APIs?
questions.answer: Established logics provide patterns for ownership/lifetime/unsafe-API composition, but actual concrete semantics adequacy and compatible client contracts remain required premises.

questions.question: What do atomics, threads, synchronization, Send/Sync, and unsafe trait implementations require?
questions.answer: Threads/atomics and unsafe Send/Sync need interference-aware sharing/transfer invariants and the selected memory model, not a sequential value contract.

questions.question: Can sequential functional reasoning compose with concurrent library contracts?
questions.answer: Sequential functional reasoning composes through explicit exclusive access, lock invariants, linearization/history or another justified concurrent contract.

questions.question: How do async lowering, suspension, cancellation, and destruction change ownership obligations?
questions.answer: Suspension stores resource-bearing state; cancellation/destruction is an additional exit requiring restoration/cleanup for every suspended state.

questions.question: What does Pin require? Should different effect domains use a common semantics or separately justified translation paths?
questions.answer: Pin concerns address-sensitive lifetime/projection/destruction invariants. Separate effect paths can share an interface only with justified concrete interpretations and relations.

questions.question: Evaluate Std.WP, vcgen and legacy mvcgen, generalized framing, and deeply embedded languages.
questions.answer: Lean4.35 Std.WP supports generalized assertion lattices, frames and deeply embedded commands. Its demonstration heap is not a Rust memory model.

questions.question: Compare those facilities with Aeneas WP/step tools, including exact specification equivalences, missing features, and performance.
questions.answer: Current Aeneas uses the legacy Std.Do bridge; exact spec=DWP and dspec=DWLP distinctions and nondivergence preconditions matter. No current adapter benchmark was run.

questions.question: Investigate partial_fixpoint, fixed-point induction, do notation, mutable locals, loops and exits; UInt/SInt/BitVec; grind/omega/bv_decide/simp; containers; Lean.Expr, quotation, and elaboration.
questions.answer: G09 maps partial/fixed-point tools, notation/control flow, scalar containers, simplification/decision procedures and elaboration to the obligations they can support.

questions.question: Which facilities help explain or verify current implementations versus generated programs? What is stable, experimental, semantically mismatched, or insufficient for borrow/resource reasoning?
questions.answer: Lean facilities can discharge logical/algorithmic obligations after interpretation and adequacy are supplied; no generic VCG or monotone WP instance establishes borrow/resource semantics.

questions.question: Compare fuel, inductive evaluation, coinductive traces, interaction trees, partiality monads, and order-theoretic fixed points.
questions.answer: Fuel, inductive judgments, coinductive traces, ITree and order-theoretic fixed points expose different termination and effect observations; select a common adequacy statement before comparing.

questions.question: Distinguish partial, partial_fixpoint, well-founded recursion, and opaque definitions.
questions.answer: partial, partial_fixpoint, well-founded recursion and opaque definitions have different logical/runtime roles; equations may underdetermine diverging executions.

questions.question: When do equations characterize behavior adequately, and how are divergence and failure separated from unspecified logical values?
questions.answer: Current ITree Result explicitly distinguishes fail/div; DWP is least-fixed-point total correctness and DWLP greatest-fixed-point partial correctness. Ordinary inhabited outputs need an independent divergence account.

questions.question: What supports extrinsic successful-termination proofs? How is compiled execution related to logical denotation?
questions.answer: Extrinsic termination proofs need a measure or semantic totality argument; logical denotation does not by itself certify compiled execution and foreign/runtime behavior.

questions.question: Survey verified compilation, proof-producing translation, result checking, per-pass validation, guided symbolic replay, and interpreter specialization.
questions.answer: G13 compares verified translation, per-run checking, proof production, hinted replay, per-pass validation and specialization by the proposition accepted.

questions.question: Which witness formats describe borrow operations, abstraction changes, joins, loop invariants, and pure transformations?
questions.answer: Proposed witnesses carry resource/identity maps for borrow/abstraction steps, injections for joins, invariants/exits for loops and typed local derivations for pure passes.

questions.question: How are checking soundness, producer completeness, failure behavior, and proof composition separated?
questions.answer: Checker soundness permits incomplete/rejecting search; acceptance must bind complete subjects and fail closed. Semantic relations need composable direction/stuttering/failure conditions.

questions.question: Compare certificate size, checking cost, implementation complexity, and assumptions using actual published systems.
questions.answer: Katamaran/CakeML/Lean4Lean provide actual published cost anchors for different workloads. Proposed Aeneas witness size/checking cost remains unknown; cross-system timing ratios would be invalid.

questions.question: Inventory axioms, opaque constants, admissions, native evaluation, unsafe code, foreign interfaces, runtime assumptions, and proof-checking paths.
questions.answer: G09 separates kernel proof checking, model adequacy, statement identity and compiled execution; nativeEqTrue adds a fresh axiom even when its caller is a proved certificate checker.

questions.question: What exactly does each selected decision procedure or certificate checker trust?
questions.answer: simp/omega/grind proof construction differs from native-backed decision paths. Audit the actual returned proof and reachable axioms, not the tactic name.

questions.question: How are unexpected assumptions and theorem dependency changes detected?
questions.answer: Dependency/axiom audits and fixed allowlists detect unexpected assumptions; source policy inspection of lake check is not an executed closure audit.

questions.question: Evaluate independent kernels, lake check, comparator-style checking, and their limitations. Separate theorem-statement correctness, proof validity, model adequacy, and execution identity.
questions.answer: Independent checkers diversify proof validity checks but retain export/theory/runtime premises; agreement does not establish source/model correspondence or correct theorem selection.

questions.question: Compare text, syntax, kernel expressions, and deeply embedded programs with denotations.
questions.answer: Text, parsed syntax, elaborated kernel terms and deeply embedded denotations are distinct output boundaries. Only the identified term has a kernel type.

questions.question: How do printer escaping, coercions, typeclass inference, notation, names, and namespaces affect output?
questions.answer: Escaping, names, coercions, notation and inferred dictionaries can change elaborated meaning. Printer success alone is not semantic identity.

questions.question: How are generated auxiliaries, recursive definitions, imports, and model lookups included?
questions.answer: Generated helpers, recursive definitions, model lookups and complete imports form the relevant closure; omitted/stub/error declarations need explicit accounting.

questions.question: What independently checkable evidence ties a theorem to the intended generated definition, source artifact, and specification?
questions.answer: Bind the intended source/IR/specification to the actual definition and semantic relation. Hashes identify bytes; checked equations/relations justify their meaning.

questions.question: Read open and closed issues, merged fixes, regression commits, release changes, disabled tests, and relevant discussions.
questions.answer: G11 samples open/closed issues, merged patches, comments, commits and test sources through a recorded bounded protocol. It is a classified technical sample, not an exhaustive issue census.

questions.question: Classify accepted semantic errors, inconsistent axioms, ill-typed output, unsupported inputs, internal failures, frontend/schema problems, and proof-performance regressions separately.
questions.answer: Accepted model errors, Rocq inconsistency, ill-typed output, unsupported input, internal/schema failures and performance cases are separate classes with exact records.

questions.question: Which fixes establish a general invariant versus patch a special case? Which required independent semantic oracles?
questions.answer: Tie-choice and Vec behavior need independent operation contracts; binder/projection repairs expose recurring invariants. A merged patch alone does not prove the general invariant.

questions.question: Audit nested borrows, projections, joins, fixed points, closure state, traits/binders, drops, partial output, models, and target interfaces; locate durable tests and missing regressions.
questions.answer: The ledger covers nested borrows/joins/closures/binders/drop/model/target cases and checks durable test paths. #1412 described path was absent in inspected trees, without claiming no equivalent test exists.

questions.question: Compare actual Rust, independent semantics/interpreters, concrete Aeneas execution, and generated models; identify shared-code dependencies between oracles.
questions.answer: Rust execution, independent semantics, concrete Aeneas and generated models have different shared dependencies. hax Lean delegation is not an independent translation oracle.

questions.question: Investigate well-typed generation, differential fuzzing, counterexample minimization, and metamorphic changes such as helper extraction, aggregate splitting, opacity, and equivalent control flow.
questions.answer: G11 derives typed-generation, minimization and metamorphic oracles with separate expected acceptance/error classifications; no fresh fuzz campaign was performed.

questions.question: Can deliberate invalid transformations exercise admission and certificate checks?
questions.answer: Prior executed CFG/byte certificates preserve deliberate bad transformations and counterexamples. They exercise narrow checks, not a complete current admission validator.

questions.question: Include target-only universe/elaboration/recursion tests and cross-model interface tests; categorize expected rejection, failure, disagreement, and performance regressions.
questions.answer: Target-only universe/elaboration/recursion sources and cross-model interfaces need separate tests from Rust execution; report rejection, internal failure, disagreement and performance distinctly.

questions.question: Measure translation, proof generation, elaboration, kernel checking, memory, certificate size, and storage separately.
questions.answer: G12 records published workload measurements, existing exact-pin component timings and a stage-specific measurement protocol. Current all-stage translation/proof/check/storage costs remain unmeasured.

questions.question: Identify quadratic structures, lost sharing, large terms, recursive groups, and proof bottlenecks.
questions.answer: Source loops/maps/sharing and generated recursive groups identify candidate bottlenecks; they are hypotheses until profiled under controlled identities.

questions.question: What correctness conditions govern caching, incremental checking, and parallelism? Which semantic, model, source, compiler, and target identities belong in cache keys?
questions.answer: Cache keys must bind semantic/source/compiler/target/configuration/model/dependency identities and proposition/checker policy. Parallel/incremental reuse cannot discard dependency closure.

questions.question: How robust are proofs and generated interfaces under small changes and toolchain upgrades? What are the maintenance costs of shared generic lemmas versus specialized proofs?
questions.answer: Small-change robustness needs regeneration/elaboration/proof/behavior observations separately. Shared generic lemmas amortize proofs but can increase dependency and specialization costs.

questions.question: Compare RustHorn/RustHornBelt, RustBelt, RefinedRust, Creusot, hax, Electrolysis, Corten, and relevant other Rust verification work.
questions.answer: G10/G13 compare RustBelt/RustHornBelt/RefinedRust/Creusot/hax/Electrolysis/Corten with exact theorem and frontend/model boundaries, reusing pinned corpus subjects.

questions.question: Examine Foundational VeriFast's hinted mirroring and Katamaran's verified symbolic execution.
questions.answer: Foundational VeriFast checks replay hints against its axiomatic semantics with admitted primitive/storage gaps; Katamaran proves symbolic-to-shallow/operational steps for its language.

questions.question: Study relevant proof-producing compiler techniques in Cogent, CompCert, CakeML, and other systems; inspect Lean-based verified-checker experience including Lean4Lean.
questions.answer: Cogent/Dargent separates value/state/layout relations; CompCert composes qualified simulations; CakeML provides verified compilation/proof synthesis; Lean4Lean checks proof objects.

questions.question: Compare precise theorem domains, semantic assumptions, reusable abstractions, certificate/proof interfaces, and measured costs rather than feature names alone.
questions.answer: The comparison records statement domains, assumptions, witness interfaces and measured tasks. Architecture labels or incomparable timing figures cannot establish a ranking.

questions.question: Which obligations are value-level, and which require bytes, layout, validity, provenance, resources, or contextual safety?
questions.answer: Anneal obligations separate layout arithmetic, byte/value validity, unsafe resources, functional behavior, Rust/assembly ABI and deployment binding.

questions.question: How do pure specifications compose with unsafe Rust bodies, opaque implementations, intrinsics, and assembly?
questions.answer: Pure specifications compose with unsafe/opaque/intrinsic/assembly bodies only through matching implementation contracts and concrete footprint/failure/resource relations.

questions.question: What interface supports Rust/assembly behavioral correspondence together with ownership and ABI requirements?
questions.answer: Rust/assembly correspondence requires argument/result encoding, register/stack/clobbers, memory/provenance, control/unwind and architectural-effect contracts tied to instruction identity.

questions.question: Which facts must survive extraction for casts, slices, initialization, alignment, and zero-copy reasoning? What TCB assumptions remain at each boundary?
questions.answer: Retain types/metadata/extents/stride/alignment/initializedness/call identity and update/resource ownership. Each erased fact needs an irrelevance theorem or exposed assumption.

questions.question: Propose and, when undertaken, preserve minimal examples for mutable-reference updates, returned borrows, nested aggregate/enum borrows, loops carrying borrows, and generics instantiated with borrowed types.
questions.answer: The eleven-case inventory proposes returned-reference, nested/enum/loop and borrowed-generic probes while reusing preserved mutable-update specimens; five cases reuse actual older executions.

questions.question: Include mutable closures returning unit, move/drop/panic behavior, safe APIs with unsafe implementations, control-flow reconstruction, historical model errors, and a small zerocopy/Anneal case.
questions.answer: Closure/unit, move/drop/panic, unsafe-safe API, CFG, model-error and zerocopy cases have distinct fixtures/oracles or explicit unperformed status.

questions.question: State each experiment's question, exact revisions/configuration, independent oracle, result classification, and limits.
questions.answer: G14 links exact configurations and evidence in the original executed packages; source/history and proposed cases are separately classified, with no new current-pin execution claimed.

questions.question: Reconcile all reports into a coverage map, explicit remaining assumptions, prioritized follow-ups, and evidence needed to resolve outstanding questions.
questions.answer: The 144-question crosswalk records answers and limits; the prioritized follow-ups expose unperformed closure audits, certificates, adapters and stronger source/resource proofs.
